text: Here is the idea of doeff, a Python library, in a minute.
doeff lets you write algebraic effects in Python.
A function asks for what it needs by yielding an effect. It never says who will answer.
The answer comes from handlers stacked outside the function.
A handler gets the effect and k, the rest of the function.
It can resume k, keep k for later, or never resume it.
Whatever it picks, k is resumed at most once.
So one function runs unchanged under many stacks. Tests, replay, bots, many at once, production.
To start, pip install doeff. Then you need three things: @do, yield, and a handler.
This article runs one card fight function under six stacks.
